title: Actress Brings African Experiences to America
main_content:
Actress Danai Gurira calls herself a Zimerican.

Her parents came from Zimbabwe. She was born in the American state of Iowa. But her family moved back to Harare, Zimbabwe, when she was five years old. She returned to the United States for college and has lived there ever since.

The actress may be best known as Michonne, the zombie–killer in the television series “The Walking Dead.” And she is now busy racing between theaters for two plays in New York City – plays that she wrote.

Her play “Familiar” centers on the cultural clashes between American and African traditions.

The play takes place in the state of Minnesota. The eldest daughter of Zimbabwean parents is getting married to a white man.

But the setting of her play “Eclipsed” — is something else entirely.

Gurira decided to write “Eclipsed” after reading a New York Times story about the civil war in Liberia, and the young women who fought in it.

Gurira went to Liberia and met with women who were former soldiers, sex slaves and peace negotiators. She wrote the play based on their stories.

questions.question: Who is Danai Gurira?
options: A theater director from Zimbabwe who focuses on American culture
An actress born in Iowa whose parents are from Zimbabwe
A playwright known for her work in Los Angeles
A film producer with no ties to Zimbabwe
questions.answer: An actress born in Iowa whose parents are from Zimbabwe

questions.question: Are the two plays similar?
options: Yes, both explore themes of African-American identity
No, one focuses on cultural clashes while the other addresses civil war
Yes, they both take place in Zimbabwe
No, they are written in different languages
questions.answer: No, one focuses on cultural clashes while the other addresses civil war
